The instant petition has been filed praying for a direction to the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner for having utilised an excess area measuring 328.50 sq.mtr. of Khasra No. 1233 of revenue village Sikandarabad Dehat, Pargana and Tehsil Sikandarabad, District Bulandshahr as per provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation Smt. sentences.text: The undisputed facts are as follows:-
The petitioner owned 0.3447 hectare of plot no. 1233.
By a notification dated 16.06.2002 issued under Section 3D of National Highways Act, 1956 an area measuring 0.017 hectare of the total area aforesaid was acquired for construction of a road by NHAI.
The award therefor was declared on 28.01.2011.
The NHAI constructed the road.

The case of the petitioner is that while constructing the road NHAI had utilised an excess area measuring 328.50 sq. mtrs. of the unacquired land and for which she is entitled to compensation as per the provisions of Act 30 of 2013.

In support of her contention she places reliance on a report of revenue team dated 10.07.2014, wherein it is recorded that on an inspection it was found that instead of 171 sq. mtrs. an area measuring 499.50 sq. mtr. had been utilised in the construction of the road.
On the basis of said report of revenue officers, the NHAI initiated proceeding for acquisition of the excess area utilised in construction of the road.
Notification under Section 3A was issued on 20 August, 2019.

Thereafter, the original record produced before us by learned counsel for NHAI reveals that some doubt was expressed with regard to the report of revenue team dated 10.07.2014 and request was made for fresh survey of the subject land.

It further appears from the record that the fresh survey was not done and in the meantime, the limitation for issuing notification under Section 3D of the Act expired and therefore, the respondents did not take any further steps for acquisition.

It is also admitted by learned counsel for NHAI that even after the limitation prescribed for issuing notification under Section 3D had expired, no fresh survey was carried out untill after the filing of the instant petition when the respondents claim to have carried out survey on 16 August, 2024 and 22 September, 2024, according to which, no excess land of plot no. 1233 was utilised in construction of the road.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contends that the survey now carried out by the respondents is wholly illegal, as they had not demarcated the remaining land of the petitioner except for mentioning in the report that no excess area was utilised in construction of the highway.

5. When Sri V.K. Singh, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of NHAI, is confronted with the said contention he concedes that in the survey report there is no finding that the remaining area of the petitioner has been demarcated and is still intact.
In fact, there is even no indication in the report that the remaining area has been duly demarcated.

6. In such circumstances, we are not inclined to accept the survey report and are of the opinion that the said issue should be determined by the District Level Committee in terms of Government Order dated 12.05.2016.

7. Sri V.K. Singh, learned Senior Counsel appearing for NHAI and Sri Rajiv Gupta, appearing for the State respondents, also have no objection in case the claim of the petitioner is considered by the Smt. sentences.text: District Level Committee in terms of aforesaid Government Order.

8. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of with the direction to the respondent no. 2 to place the claim of the petitioner before the District Level Committee for being decided in terms of Government Order dated 12 May, 2016 within twelve weeks from the date of communication of the instant order along with a fresh representation.

It is desirable that the District Level Committee before taking any decision in the matter, gets a fresh survey conducted by a joint survey team comprising of the revenue officials and representative of NHAI other than those who had earlier carried out the survey, in presence of the petitioner or her representative.
9. The survey team will demarcate the remaining area of the petitioner, as available on the spot and will specify whether entire area (unacquired) is still available or any part had been utilised.
The petitioner would be given opportunity of hearing before any decision is taken.

It is clarified that no observation made herein would influence the decision of District Level Committee to be taken in compliance of the instant order except to the extent of the directions that have been issued in respect of the manner in which survey is to be conducted.
10. The original record has been returned to Sri V.K. Singh, learned Senior Counsel appearing for NHAI.
(Manish Kumar Nigam, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.)
